statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.answer: No. 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires suspicious activity reporting by a “financial institution,” and the facts do not establish that SYN_79cdbb28 is a covered financial institution or that any such institution detected and was required to report the activity.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) authorizes/mandates that a “financial institution” file a suspicious activity report (SAR) when it detects a suspicious transaction relevant to a possible violation of law or regulation, and it provides a safe harbor and confidentiality for such reports. Element-by-element: (1) Covered actor: § 5318(g) applies to a “financial institution” (as defined under the BSA framework). The fact pattern identifies SYN_79cdbb28 as a convenience/grocery store business, not as a bank/MSB/broker-dealer/other covered financial institution, and it does not identify any bank or other financial institution involved as the reporting entity. Therefore it is not established that § 5318(g) applies to this entity. (2) Triggering condition: § 5318(g) concerns detection of “suspicious” transactions; while the listed transactions include large cash/card/ACH/wire activity, the facts do not state that any financial institution detected suspicion or that the activity was suspicious under applicable SAR rules. Because the necessary predicate facts are missing, applicability cannot be determined. Contiguous phrase in answer: “31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires”.
